meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why was Owen's grade entered before anyone called me?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. And the zero itself? On what basis was it entered?

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
Someone can draft in another program and move it over. Put the version history in front of me, with the dates on it, not your description of it. And did you speak to Owen before you entered anything?
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Then pull it up. And you haven't told me whether you spoke to Owen before the zero.
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
A student can misremember a line from a play. Turn the screen so I can see the history first. And you still haven't said whether anyone spoke to Owen before that zero went in.
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay. That's called revising. Put the version history in front of me, then we'll do the rest one at a time.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
A seventeen-year-old asked a vocabulary question cold isn't a transcript. Show me the note you wrote. And I still haven't seen the history.
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
A forty-minute in-class piece and a weekend essay aren't the same task. You've now described four things and shown me none. Turn the screen, Hale.
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Good, because the company that sells it says it can't be the sole basis for anything against a student. So the history is what you have. Turn the screen.
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.
That's 4.4, and I want it in writing, today, with the zero out of the gradebook until then. But I'm agreeing to nothing while I've still seen nothing on paper or on a screen.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Not yet. You offered to pull up the history, so pull it up. Then I'll answer you.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
Ten minutes. I'm not picking a day for something I haven't agreed to. The history is on your screen; turn it.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
The writing tonight, yes. Nothing else is agreed, because I still haven't seen a single document. Turn the screen.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
The version history, on the screen, now. And the note from November 2.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still need the version history shown to me, the note from November 2, and your offer confirmed to me in writing, with the zero out of the gradebook until then. I expect that in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position and agreed to nothing, and she still wants the version history and your November 2 note put in front of her, your offer in writing tonight, and the zero out of the gradebook until then; the fair outcome is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and you reached the offer but not the evidence that would have let her accept it.

What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling her in one plain sentence, and it earned a flat Okay, because it answered her procedural complaint without a defence.

What cost ground: You described your evidence several times and never showed it, so every piece stayed a claim she could meet with one defence, and offering the rewrite before any of it was in front of her made it sound like a bargain.

What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your edit times of 11:31, 11:52 and 11:58 PM on October 28 came very close to that night, which is why she got shorter and harder; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.

Try next time: Right after she first asked to see the history, turn the screen and walk her through the edit times before mentioning the quotation, the outline, or 4.4.
